A1.justification: Both PDFs describe MCMARK and contain complete, readable main texts and Appendices A–D. Text extraction and rendered-page comparison support reliable comparison of the equations, figures and tables.

before.justification: v2 reports original generation-quality, watermark-detection, attack-robustness and channel-count experiments in Section 5 and Appendix D.

after.justification: v3 retains the original empirical evaluations in Section 5 and Appendix D, including Tables 1–7 and Figures 3–11.

M1.justification: v3 divides Equation 3's off-diagonal channel probabilities by sum_k(1 - l P_Vk)_+, which v2 omits. This corrects the reweighting specified through Algorithm 1 while retaining the channel framework and detector. The PDFs do not establish whether the experimental implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both versions retain the same generation, summarization and translation coverage: C4, MMW, Dolly CW, WaterBench, CNN/DailyMail and WMT16 ro-en. The attack scenarios are also unchanged.

E2.justification: The unwatermarked baseline, KGW, Unigram, ITS-edit, EXP-edit, γ-reweight, DiPmark and STA-1 retain the same participation and configurations in the corresponding comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix C retain the same models, 1,000 examples per task, evaluation metrics, channel-count sweeps and attack settings. No revised evaluation protocol or experimental rerun is reported.

E4.justification: The token-replacement, GPT rephrasing, GPT back-translation and DIPPER analyses are unchanged. The channel-count sensitivity and detectability–robustness studies in Figures 5–6 and 8–11 are also identical.

E5.justification: Run and seed disclosures, statistical reporting practices, Figure 3's distribution plots and detection p-value reporting are unchanged. Neither version adds uncertainty estimates or statistical comparison procedures.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 and empirical Figures 3–11 retain identical results. For example, Table 1 reports MCMARK's TPR of 98.38% at FPR 0.1% in both versions; Appendix Tables 6–7 retain perplexity 6.3864 and BLEU 20.16.

T1.justification: Equation 3's normalization corrects the constructive solution to Equation 2: for nonuniform segment masses, it restores channel normalization and unbiasedness constraints that v2's formula can violate. The objective, bounds and other derivations, including Appendix B, are unchanged. v3 leaves the equal-mass, zero-denominator case unspecified.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same claims of unbiased watermarking, model-agnostic detection, improved robustness and over 10% detectability improvement. The normalization correction does not revise the stated contributions.

C2.justification: The interpretations of detectability, robustness and channel-count effects are unchanged, including Appendix B and the Limitations paragraph. No explanatory qualification accompanies the normalization correction.

D1.justification: Appendix C's implementation settings and hyperparameters, the efficiency discussion and the code-availability statement are unchanged. No additional implementation guidance or resource-access information is supplied.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and reference list are identical, including the positioning relative to DiPmark, STA-1 and other unbiased watermarks.

P1.justification: The arXiv version/date stamp changes from v2, 3 July 2025, to v3, 6 August 2025. The prose, terminology, section order and appendix organization are otherwise unchanged.

P2.justification: Figure 2's embedded formula gains the same normalization denominator as Equation 3. The taller equation causes limited spacing and text-flow changes on pages 4–5. Other figures and all table layouts remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The focused normalization correction improves mathematical consistency and reproducibility. Using Figure 1's 0.3/0.7 segment masses, v2's Equation 3 gives channel 1 a total probability of 0.76, whereas v3 gives 1. The repair remains incomplete because equal segment masses produce an unspecified 0/0 case in v3. The empirical evidence is unchanged.
